claim_class: Inherited compact primitive fallback in a self-contained positive-cost formulation, not a new dark-space criterion.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: Uniform finite-cost feasibility for arbitrary visible history is equivalent to absence of a closed common dark subspace in every fixed model and to properness of every one-row full-support command policy; its resolvent gives finite cap C0.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
label: thm:r79-dark-feasibility
limits: The all-initial-state and all-commands-legal requirements are essential. Does not decide partial-prior reachability or optional commitment.
proof: If a dark space exists, every policy stays there. Otherwise a spectral-radius-one full-support failure map has a positive nonzero Cesaro fixed point whose support is common and dark. Inverse continuity on the compact family bounds the one-row cost.
title: Feasibility from arbitrary initial quantum states

classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: The support of the sum of T^n iota_1(I), 0<=n<=Md-1, is the least invariant corner. Finite all-initial cost implies finite cost and transience on that corner.

label: lem:r79-reachable-corner
limits: No full-space transience at inaccessible labels or physical directions.
proof: Increasing supports stabilize by finite rank. A positive finite reachability sum dominates a multiple of its support projection. Its cost is a finite sum of tails of the initial cost series; the positive cost floor then makes all restricted powers tend to zero.
title: Finite reachable-support construction

claim_class: Inherited support-potential theorem specialized to positive-cost success stopping; no separate novelty claim.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: Cost <=b for every initial density matrix iff a supported invariant projection P and positive potential W satisfy the displayed Lyapunov inequality and W_1<=bI. The least reachable true cost witness satisfies equality.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
Fixed controller, fixed model, finite proposed cost bound b.
label: thm:r79-exact-certificate
limits: A global all-label inequality is not necessary before regularization.
proof: Iterating a positive supersolution bounds every finite prefix and hence the full cost. Conversely, restrict the geometric cost series to the reachable corner; the all-state initial bound is exactly the first-block operator bound.
title: Exact finite support and Lyapunov certificate

claim_class: Consolidation of inherited finite-model synthesis and compactness, extending compact semialgebraic uncertainty to unrestricted legal feedback. The distinct central addition is subsequent same-memory stability.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: Every finite-M robust optimum is attained and nonincreasing in M. Its exact certificate has order exists common controller, for every fixed model, exists model-specific P,W. Algebraic primitive families give an algebraic value and attaining algebraic controller by finite real elimination.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
No model has a closed dark subspace. For the effective clause: a compact semialgebraic parameter set and algebraic polynomial/rational primitive coefficients with no poles.
label: thm:r79-quantum-frontier
limits: No efficient algorithm, executed general QE, attained worst model, universal closed form or finite saturation of unrestricted history.
proof: The robust objective is a supremum of continuous finite-prefix objectives, hence lower semicontinuous on a compact controller simplex. The support certificate is applied modelwise with the same controller. Real/imaginary coordinates and PSD principal minors give a quantified semialgebraic formula; the attained finite endpoint and sample controller are algebraic.
title: Robust quantum finite-memory frontier

claim_class: Explicit positive-probability boundary example for the reset same-row theorem, not an all-controller two-row optimum or general POMDP novelty claim.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: A uniform initial row followed by pure alternating rows costs 34/11, below the one-row robust value 10/3. Every report-only deterministic routing of that same palette costs at least 10/3. The known-model qubit lift has the same all-initial-state values.
hypotheses: Two scalar hidden models with success probabilities (1/2,1/10) and their swap; unit costs, one failure report, fixed hidden model and counted pure initializer.
The same example is lifted to a known nonreset qubit instrument with diagonal failure Kraus operators.
label: ex:r79-hidden-model-memory
limits: The three-label value is an achievable upper bound, not a claimed exact V3 for this example. Physical reset with unknown fixed model differs from a known reset state sufficient for control.
proof: Compute the two alternating Bellman recurrences exactly and minimize the single-row worst cost. For report-only routing a single destination row is used after all failures. Diagonal qubit costs and branch traces depend only on the diagonal initial mixture, whose extremes are the two models.
title: Information remains after a physical reset

claim_class: Explicit compact boundary obstruction motivating same-memory regularization.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: Initial cost is 2-theta for theta>0 and 1 at theta=0, with unattained supremum 2. For 0<theta<1 the reachable second-label true cost is 1/theta; no uniform original-witness bound exists.
hypotheses: Scalar compact family theta in [0,1], unit costs; failure of a is theta(1-theta), failure of b is 1-theta.
Start at a then stay at b after failure, with the initial label counted.
label: ex:r79-unbounded-reachable-witness
limits: Does not contradict initial robust boundedness, attained minimization over controllers, or regularized global witness bounds.
proof: Sum the geometric tail after the first failure. At theta=0 the second label is dark but inaccessible; at theta=1 it is also inaccessible. Every interior second label is reachable and has reciprocal-theta cost.
title: Finite initial cost with unbounded continuation witnesses

claim_class: Principal new resource-preserving construction: no additional label, no physical reset, uniform over a fixed hidden model. It is distinct from inherited finite-prefix completion with growing memory.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: The same command rows and M labels have initial cost <=U=b/(1-epsilon*b/c_*) and cost <=K=c^*/epsilon+U from every physical state at every label. Full-space exact cost witnesses obey these bounds.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
An M-label controller has robust all-initial cost <=b. After each failure, independently return its label to 1 with probability epsilon; 0<epsilon<=1 and epsilon*b<c_*.
internal_load_bearing_facts: Finiteness proved from finite restart generations; no circular inequality with an infinite expected cost.
The restart coin writes the existing initial label and leaves the physical posterior untouched.
label: thm:r79-label-restart
limits: Requires the all-initial-state cost guarantee. The hidden model never changes during execution; command rows remain identical but update probabilities change. The constants are upper bounds without sharpness claim.
proof: Cut each label-1 segment at success or its first restart coin. Its cost is <=b and restart probability <=epsilon*b/c_*. Bound finite numbers of segments by a geometric sum, then use monotone convergence. From any label the first segment costs <=c^*/epsilon; after a restart the label-1 bound applies. Positive-cost transience gives full-space cost operators.
title: Regularization with the same live-label budget

claim_class: Inherited centered trace estimate in the controller-block setting; a supporting transfer lemma, not a new general norm inequality.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: The adjoint continuation error is bounded in order by eta*K I. If delta=zeta+eta*K<c_*, scaling W by 1/(1-delta/c_*) gives a target global supersolution.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
The same counted controller in two models; a source global witness 0<=W_k<=KI.
Normalized output includes success, with instrument half-trace distance <=eta; cost operator distance <=zeta; target has positive cost floor c_*.
label: lem:r79-centered-perturbation
limits: Requires bounded global witnesses, not only bounded initial cost. The success outcome cannot be omitted in the centered estimate.
proof: The difference of normalized full output states has zero trace. Center its bounded block observable at K I/2, including zero success observable. Transfer the source supersolution and use the target positive-cost floor to absorb its scalar error by scaling.
title: Perturbation of a bounded cost witness

claim_class: Principal new theorem: a complete optimal-frontier modulus uniform in all counted memory budgets, with same-size controllers and nonreset quantum back-action. Search found no exact matching theorem; priority and top-journal significance remain subject to independent assessment.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: The target M-label value is <=U_epsilon/[1-(zeta+eta*K_epsilon)/c_*]. Under the displayed smallness assumptions every M simultaneously satisfies |V_M(U)-V_M(V)| <= ((10B^2+4Bc^*)/c_*)*sqrt(eta)+(4B/c_*)*zeta. This holds across changes in supports and extends to eta=0.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
A feasible source compact model family. Each target model pairs with one source model satisfying both distance bounds; pairing is only an offline proof choice.
For two-sided uniformity both families have a common one-row cap B and cost bounds, with explicit smallness conditions on eta,zeta.
internal_load_bearing_facts: Identical source/target controller parameters, with witnesses allowed to vary across paired models.
Constants do not depend on M; both cost lower bounds and one-row B are explicit.
label: thm:r79-frontier-stability
limits: The exponent is not claimed optimal. Family matching is not adversarial switching, model revelation, optional commitment or a restricted-prior theorem.
proof: Regularize one attaining common source controller without adding memory. Transfer its bounded full-space witnesses model by model. The same probabilities implement all target models. Set epsilon=sqrt(eta), bound U<=2B and delta<=c_*/2, and reverse directions. Treat eta=0 by taking epsilon down to zero. Local properness of a fixed full-support row supplies common neighborhood caps.
title: Uniform stability of the complete memory frontier

claim_class: Inherited completion mechanism with explicit cost and memory count; the extension of the new uniform modulus to its limit is a consequence.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: V_M decreases to the unrestricted visible-history infimum. With M_T=1+sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(|A||Y|)^t, V_M_T <= V_hist*(1+C0/(c_*T)). The same uniform stability bound holds for V_hist.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.
All commands legal; mandatory immediate success stopping; common positive mean cost bounds c_* I <= G <= c^* I.
One autonomous model-independent classical controller, prescribed pure initial label counted, no uncounted clock/history/seed, and worst cost over every initial density matrix.
The compact model family is feasible with full-support one-row cap C0.
label: cor:r79-history-limit
limits: No exact finite saturation or efficient history tree. Model-independent visible-history kernels have no undeclared observation port.
proof: Store the first T command/report pairs in counted history-tree labels and then use one additional fallback label. Positive cost bounds survival by b/(c_*T); all-initial fallback handles the actual posterior. Infimize without assuming an optimal unrestricted policy and pass the uniform-in-M stability bound to the limit.
title: Finite-memory approximation to unrestricted control

claim_class: Exact special-model all-M law and counted-initializer separation; not a general closed quantum frontier.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness
Classical reachability, cost-potential verification and stochastic controller theory, as individually attributed in the manuscript
conclusion: Exactly V1=2, V2=(1+sqrt(5))/2, and V_M=3/2 for M>=3, which also equals the unrestricted visible-history optimum. The two-label optimizer has model-specific supports (1,0) and (1,1).
hypotheses: Two fixed hidden scalar models: command a succeeds surely only in model 0, b surely only in model 1; other calls fail, unit costs and one failure report.
Arbitrary randomized updates allowed; one pure initial live label is counted.
internal_load_bearing_facts: In model 0 label 2 is inaccessible and dark; forcing a full-space potential produces the impossible inequality W_2>=1+W_2.
label: prop:r79-golden-ratio-memory
limits: A free mixed initializer changes the resource problem and attains 3/2 with two labels. The zero-success degeneracy is explicit; the separate positive example tests a different structural boundary.
proof: One label minimizes max(1/r,1/(1-r)). For two label rows r,s, split r>=s and r<=s; maximal conditional success gives reciprocal bounds, while failure of the first call gives affine bounds. Balancing max(1/r,1+r) gives the golden ratio, attained by the explicit transition rule. Any first command incurs worst cost at least 3/2; three labels attain it.
title: Golden-ratio memory cost

claim_class: A quantitative refinement in a stronger structural class, using the classical resolvent perturbation mechanism; no claim that this classical mechanism is novel or the general square-root exponent is sharp.
classical_ingredients: Positive-map norm contraction and the resolvent identity
Geometric waiting-time cost and conditional survival bounds
conclusion: All M simultaneously satisfy |V_M(U)-V_M(V)|<=zeta/kappa+c^* eta/kappa^2 without small-error restriction; the same holds for V_hist. Counted history completion has error at most C0(1-kappa)^T. Scalar geometric waiting proves local sharpness of both coefficients for 0<kappa<1.
hypotheses: Same finite-dimensional primitive interface and positive-cost conventions, with common cost ceiling c^*.
For every command and model in both compared compact families, success effect B_a>=kappa I with fixed 0<kappa<=1.
Mutual model pairing simultaneously bounds normalized instrument and cost distances by eta and zeta.
internal_load_bearing_facts: The full adjoint map contracts the Hermitian block norm by 1-kappa for every controller.
The scalar exact difference zeta/kappa+C eta/[kappa(kappa+eta)] gives matching local coefficients independently of M.
label: cor:r79-positive-success
limits: Uniform per-command success is stronger than common-dark-space exclusion. Exponential approximation is in history horizon, generally a power law in the number of history labels. Coefficient sharpness is local and does not classify support-degenerate instruments.
proof: Bound every full-space inverse by 1/kappa and every positive cost witness by c^*/kappa. Subtract the two fixed-controller cost equations, apply the centered estimate, then take model suprema and controller infima. Uniform success gives a geometric survival tail for counted prefix completion. Solve the scalar geometric waiting laws to prove sharpness.
title: Positive-success refinement
